title: Don’t mind me, just thinking about Ragtime again #theatre #broadway
transcript: Why do some characters in ragtime have names like Sarah and coalhouse, and some of them have, like, familiar names like father and mother and Tateh? Now, the surface answer is that this is a holdover from the novel of which the musical is based off of. But the answer, I feel, goes even deeper than that. Part of this is definitely because the story itself is being told by Edgar. Edgar's The Little Boy. He starts the show, he ends the show. So much of this is him telling the story of this thing that happened at the turn of the century. And so we have all these historical figures that are important to his childhood, that were made an impact on the time period. But we also have all of the familial people that are just really important to him. They're not necessarily important to the broader story, except for Sarah and CoalHouse, before I go on, I do think it's important for me to give, like, a major spoiler warning. So if you have not seen ragtime and you want to go in blind or experience it blind the first time, major, major, major, major, major spoiler warning right here. This is your last warning. But Sarah and coalhouse are historical figures to Edgar. They're fictional characters to us, but they are important historical characters that deserve to be named in this story in the same way that we say the Names of people who have been brutalized by police to this day. Sarah and coalhouse may be fictional characters, but for the story of ragtime, it is important to remember their names. And because of Sarah and Coalhouse’s tragic endings, I think it's important to give them names as characters so that they don't become representative of an entire demographic. We don't want them to be representative of every black man and black woman. Compare that to a character like mother, who becomes representative of an entire group of white women during this time period right before women's suffrage, where they were kind of starting to open their eyes to the world around them and wanting to step more into their own, away from their husbands. Compare that to the generic story of Tateh, a very much a success story of an immigrant who's able to come to America and find that American dream that he's been striving for. Sarah and coalhouse don't get that success. Their lives are cut tragically short. And therefore, we get names for them. We remember them, we acknowledge their stories and how they affect the narrative. Because of that, because their stories end in the confines of ragtime, I think it's important that they become historical figures of this story, even though they are fictional. But I also think it's important that we give them names so they don't become emblematic of all black women and black men. That this is Not their story. These are two specific stories of these two people that had a great effect on the lives around them. That's personally how I choose to interpret why Sarah and coalhouse have names and the other characters do not. But I'm curious, what is your interpretation?
